title: Selimiye Mosque, Edirne
summary: The Selimiye Mosque in Edirne, Turkey, was built for Sultan Selim II by the architect Sinan between 1568 and 1575. Its single great dome, about 31 metres across, rests on eight supports and is flanked by four tall minarets. Sinan regarded it as his masterpiece.

uncertainty.note: Turkey's Ministry of Culture and Tourism gives 1568-1575; the ICOMOS evaluation gives 1569-75. End is the present.

as_recorded.value: It was built in Edirne during 1568-1575 by architect Mimar Sinan upon the orders of Sultan Selim II.

where.modern_name: Selimiye Mosque and Social Complex, Edirne, Türkiye

importance.justification: Sinan's own chosen masterpiece, a UNESCO World Heritage mosque whose single dome set a benchmark in Ottoman domed architecture.
